aula.titulo: Review and test of the first block
aula.objetivo: Review pronunciation, articles, the present tense, the accusative, separable verbs, time and directions, correct the most common mistakes of English speakers and take the test of the first block.

blocos.texto: Goal of the lesson. By the end of the four sessions, you ask yes/no questions and questions with wer, was, wo, woher, wohin, wann and wie, and answer in full sentences.

blocos.contexto: Camila is in the classroom. The teacher takes attendance. Jonas sits next to her.

linhas.ru: — Aus Brasilien. Ich wohne jetzt in München.
linhas.en: — From Brazil. Now I live in Munich.
linhas.audio: Aus Brasilien. Ich wohne jetzt in München.

linhas.ru: — Hallo, ich bin Jonas. Wo wohnst du?
linhas.en: — Hi, I am Jonas. Where do you live?
linhas.audio: Hallo, ich bin Jonas. Wo wohnst du?

linhas.ru: — Cool! Ich auch. Trinken wir nachher Kaffee?
linhas.en: — Cool! Me too. Shall we have a coffee later?
linhas.audio: Cool! Ich auch. Trinken wir nachher Kaffee?

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: There is a second trap. English often uses “where” for two ideas (“Where are you?” and “Where are you going?”). German separates three: STEP 2: wo stationary, wohin with movement to there, woher with movement from there.
blocos.comparacao: In English, a yes/no question is built with «do» or by swapping the verb and the subject: “Do you live in Munich?” In German, there is no «do»: the verb simply goes to the first position: Wohnst du in München?

blocos.titulo: Everything you already know, in one table
blocos.explicacao: This table sums up lessons 1 to 9 in one line per point. Re-read one line at a time and say an example of your own out loud. If something seems strange, go back to the lesson indicated or open the topic in the Grammar tab.

tabela.rule: ei = «eye», ie = long «ee», sch = «sh», ch = «ç» or «kh», w = «v», v = «f», z = «ts», s + vowel = «z».
The conjugated verb stays in 2nd position; the yes/no question starts with the verb.
ich bin, du bist, er ist...; ich habe, du hast, er hat...
du (one friend), ihr (several friends), Sie (formal, one or several).
der, die, das; every noun with a capital letter; learn the article with the word.
Five types: -e, -(e)n, -er, no ending, -s (often with an umlaut).
ein Tisch, eine Lampe, kein Buch; in the plural, keine.
mein, meine...: they agree with the thing owned.
am Montag, im Mai, der 5. Oktober.
Only the masculine changes: der → den, ein → einen, kein → keinen.
du isst, er liest, du nimmst.
ich möchte … + second verb in the infinitive, at the end.
Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.

blocos.enunciado: Introduce yourself in 8 sentences, out loud: name, origin, age, family, where you live, what you eat, the time you get up and how you get to work.
Read out loud the alphabet and the combinations ei, ie, eu, au, sch, ch, sp, st.
